text:
emma: kicking off canary publish for python-sdk @ PyPI: 1.4.0-beta and @npm: ts-sdk 2.3.0-canary. change window tonight 22:00-23:00 UTC. tagging @martin @sara for rollout + rollback plan.

deploy-bot: canary publish started: https://ci.example.com/build/1987 (jobs: publish-py, publish-ts)

martin: saw a failing integration test in publish-py job — sending logs.

martin: failure looks like the new streaming patch broke chunked responses for sync client.

sara: ack. can we feature-flag streaming for the sync client? if not, we should roll python back.

emma: agreed. holding TS canary pending py resolution. tyler please hold the npm publish job.

tyler: npm job paused.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered for package python-sdk 1.4.0-beta -> 1.3.2 (auto)

emma: next steps: revert the streaming change in the sync wrapper, run unit+integration, republish canary. We should also add a deprecation note for legacy sync behavior in release notes.

maya: quick note for release notes: 'Deprecated legacy sync client behavior in favor of unified async-compatible streaming. Customers should pin to python-sdk==1.3.* until migration completed.'

emma: add sample pin snippet in release notes and support ticket template.

martin: patch ready: revert sync-streaming flag default to false. running tests locally, will push a PR for canary in ~20m.

sara: once PR merged, I can trigger publish. remind: change window ends 23:00 UTC — we need canary out 30m before to validate.

emma: SGTM. also updating CHANGELOG.md with deprecation header + migration steps and adding a small note in docs sdk/upgrade.md.

tyler: when we republish, ensure npm tag uses 'canary' (npm dist-tag add) and we keep semver bump minor only if fix. we'll keep TS at 2.3.0-canary but not promoted.

emma: also ping support with canned message and #support-customers DM list.

deploy-bot: publish succeeded for python-sdk 1.4.0-beta (canary) — 1763829650

emma: validating production integration now; if anything odd we roll to 1.3.2. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
